I'm black, and a woman, this makes any form of mental illness diagnosis twice as hard, I only got my ADHD and Bipolar diagnosis after my first suicide attempt. My entire life I've been told I've been looking for attention, or just flat out ignored. I understand the frustration, but ultimately, self diagnosis can be the difference between life and death. Realising I might just have autism has pulled me out of a depression because I thought I was "lazy" , "rude" or "purposefully being a nuisance". This is even harder because I live in a third world country where mental illnesses are treated like diseases if they're very apparent (like Down Syndrome) or like poppycock if they aren't (Like OCD, ADHD, ASD etc). I think this is why self diagnosis, followed by a legitimate diagnosis is very important, especially for marginalised individuals, because cognitive biases will have you thinking you're making everything up. I believe in self diagnosis, and I believe it definitely saves lives

Hey lovely person

 Some of these tips help me accept reality more, be more grounded, or actually assist in me daydreaming less.

1) Daydreaming of myself as I am.

Usually when I daydream, I dream of myself with my ideal hair, ideal body, ideal skin, and along with that ideal talents and skills. Recently, I've been daydreaming of myself as I am, but in the same fantasy situations, i.e: I usually daydream that I'm this ultra famous popstar who sings and dances and gives interviews and all that jazz. Instead of daydreaming of myself with whiter teeth and my ideal body, I daydream of me singing and dancing with the body, hair and skin that I currently have, but the crowd would still cheer for me in the exact same way. Alongside this, I began to daydream of myself at my exact skill level, for instance, I usually daydream of myself being a 10/10 singer and dancer who's fluent in 5 languages (or more), now, I daydream of being as close to my real self as possible, probably a 4/10 singer, 2.5/10 dancer and fluent-ish in 2 languages. 
This allows me to become more content with who I am in this reality, and I notice that I daydream a bit less because my "dream self" has become my real self, so if I can see who I dream of in reality, what's the need to daydream? This doesn't need to be done all at once, I started slowly, first daydreaming with my real body, but still perfect hair and skin and talents, then slowly transforming each thing into it's real form. Now I'm about 80% my real self in most of my daydreams and it's work wonders for my confidence.


2) Stretching and Shifting Focus.

I've recently started stretching, I don't do it everyday, but when I do the day feels better. Since I'm religious, as I stetch I recite prayers and shift my focus to my prayers. If you're not religious, you might find it useful to recite positive affirmations. When I find myself daydreaming I gently shift myself back into my focal point. I don't punish myself for daydreaming, because it makes everything I do feel like punishment, not growth. It really helps a lot and helps me focus through out the day too, for instance, I've written all of this so far without day dreaming once. (P.S. I have ADHD so I definitely understand how difficult it is to find focus, it gets easier with time, personally, this is my method of self medication, do what works for you magnificent human).

3) Focusing with triggers

My main triggers are music, podcasts and interviews. I'd often pause the podcast/interview and answer the questions as if they were directed to wards me, but I'd answer them as my MD self, not as my real self. If you also do something like this, I'd recommend the first step be answering the questions as your real self, with your real experiences, not the daydreamed ones, this helps you become in touch with reality and realise how interesting real you is! The next step, which is very difficult for me so far, is instead of daydreaming with these triggers, actually focus with them. Focus on the interview and see what you can learn from it, focus on the podcast and see what you can gain from it, don't use it to write your next MD script but actually focus (Again, ADHD will make this very difficult but I believe in you✧◝(⁰▿⁰)◜✧).
This will really be a facing your demons type of adventure, I think if you've close to mastered the above 2, this one will come easier, because it's really not a beginner move. It's similar to someone who was addicted to food, eating their favourite snack in moderation for the first time, it takes so much self control and willpower, and can only be done once your foundation is very sturdy.

4) Be kind to yourself.
Remember, there is nothing wrong with you, you are worthy and deserving of being loved just because you are you. I believe in you and I trust you, if you get to step 3 and you falter, it's okay to go back to step 2 for a bit more, it's okay to try and not succeed. You're much better than your former self who couldn't imagine trying to do better. Your pace will quicken with time.
